title: Mintive Raises $11M for AI Agent Identity and Spending Control Platform
summary:
The startup Mintive has introduced a security layer that provides autonomous AI agents with unique identities, preventing them from automatically inheriting the access rights of the employees who create them. The company announced the product's release alongside the closing of $11M in total funding, with Cowboy Ventures leading the most recent investment round.

The platform allows enterprises to set token budgets, monitor model costs and results, and scan tool calls for prompt injections. Mintive said its governance tools enabled Modern Treasury to implement a bank-operations agent in less than three weeks, which reduced a process that typically took four hours to several minutes.

selectedTweets.text:
MINTIVE LAUNCHES TO CONTROL WHAT AI AGENTS CAN ACCESS, DO & SPEND

They are announcing $11M in total funding, with Cowboy Ventures leading its latest round.

The platform gives each agent its own identity and permissions. Companies can approve specific tools and disable risky actions without granting everything the person setting up the agent can access.

Teams can choose which models are allowed, set budgets and automatically stop new model calls when spending limits are reached.

Tool calls are checked for prompt injection and unsafe operations. An audit trail connects each call to the person, agent, server and model involved, with visibility into costs and results.

Shared Slack agents adjust their access based on the channel and who’s asking, rather than carrying the same permissions into every conversation.

Mintive says Modern Treasury deployed a bank-operations agent in under three weeks, cutting a four-hour task to minutes.
